clue.text: Court's risen, interrupting encouraging cry from eight people?

indicators.note: the court and risen pieces break into the middle of the cry, splitting it in two

parts.note: OLE is the Spanish shout of encouragement heard at bullfights
something that has risen is up

explanation.surface: A courtroom rises while a crowd cheers, as if a group of eight people were shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Court's is read as 'is': the court is UP. The question mark flags that 'eight people' stretches a word meaning eightfold.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means eightfold, so a group of eight people could be described playfully as an eightfold set.

clue.text: Charity's repute mostly resting on livestock item? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece resting on another sits above it

parts.note: an ox is one head of livestock; the instruction to reverse things means the animal goes on top, not below

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the repute word is dropped

parts.note: fame is good repute

explanation.surface: A charity's reputation depends mainly on livestock gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, repute sits on top of the animal; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so the beast comes first in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a well-known British-founded international aid charity.

clue.text: Heat around day can upset fungal growth

indicators.note: the heat word wraps around the letter for day

parts.note: to toast something is to heat it

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means the lavatory word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: can and loo are both slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Warming a tin for a day leads to mould growing.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella-shaped fungus, especially a poisonous one, is popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Dirty election, with one politician getting off charge

parts.note: a poll is an election

indicators.note: the one and politician letters get off, removed from the charge word

parts.note: to impute is to charge or attribute something to someone
I is the Roman numeral for one
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sleazy election in which a politician escapes a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting off' sounds like acquittal, but it removes I and MP from IMPUTE, leaving UTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make something dirty or contaminated is to pollute it.

clue.text: That French woman seizes one in Britain, chasing one ready for marriage

indicators.note: the French pronoun takes hold of the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: elle is French for she, that woman

indicators.note: the second one comes first, followed by the Britain piece that chases it

parts.note: I again stands for one, as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: the first one sits inside the abbreviation for Britain

parts.note: GB is short for Great Britain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman grabs an eligible man in Britain, chasing a prospective spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'one's are placed in reverse of clue order: the one inside Britain chases the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An eligible bachelor is someone regarded as a desirable, suitable match for marriage.

clue.text: Storm encountered on the way back — a nuisance

indicators.note: travelling back means the word for encountered is read from right to left

parts.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them
a pest is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: A traveller meets a storm on the return journey, and it is a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a violent storm with strong winds is a tempest.

clue.text: Drunk, going over, experienced striking head and threw up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going over means the drunkard word flips upwards, reversed

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

indicators.note: striking out the head means removing the first letter of the experienced word

parts.note: to be used to something is to be experienced in it

explanation.surface: A drunk falls over, hits their head and is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threw up' looks like vomiting, but here it means flung into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something upwards, like a coin or a ball, is to toss it.

clue.text: Showtime at cinema is a point grasped by the writer

indicators.note: the writer's word holds the other pieces in its grip, around them

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, who is ME
a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork

explanation.surface: The writer explains when a film is showing at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon performance at a theatre or cinema is called a matinee.

clue.text: Bacterium apparent in upset that is blocked by firm line

indicators.note: the firm and line letters block the gap inside the reversed pair, sitting between its letters
in a down answer, upset means the abbreviation for that is written upwards

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A bacterium shows up in an upset stomach, blocked by a firm's production line.
explanation.definitionFit: A common gut bacterium, some strains of which cause food poisoning, bears this name.

clue.text: Sign of nervousness about English celebrity, not entirely good on the screen

indicators.note: the twitch word goes around the English and celebrity pieces

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter of the celebrity word is dropped

parts.note: a legend is a famous person

explanation.surface: An English star shows signs of nerves despite being good on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone who looks attractive or comes across well on television.

clue.text: Weaknesses in following transport obligations

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
rail is a means of transport
ties are bonds or obligations

explanation.surface: Someone admits shortcomings in keeping up with their duties about transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: moral or physical failings are frailties.

clue.text: Some steps heading off unwanted visitor to website

indicators.note: the leading letter of the walk word is removed, as if its head were cut away

parts.note: a stroll is a short walk, some leisurely steps

explanation.surface: Taking a few steps away from an intruder on a website.
explanation.definitionFit: On the internet, a person who posts provocative messages to disrupt a site is called a troll.

clue.text: Rhyme scheme offering 'line' instead of 'nine'?

parts.note: in verse, lines ending on a stressed syllable have one kind of ending, those on an unstressed syllable the feminine kind; the word for the first kind closes in L-I-N-E, while 'feminine' closes in N-I-N-E

explanation.surface: A poetic rhyme scheme that swaps one word for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is literal: of the two gendered names for line endings, one finishes with the letters LINE and its opposite, feminine, finishes with NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody this is a line ending on a stressed syllable, the opposite of a feminine ending, so it is a real term of verse.

clue.text: What's not initially encompassed by 'special' and 'delightful'?

definitions.text: What's not initially encompassed by 'special' and 'delightful'?

indicators.note: the first letter of not sits inside the word for delightful, surrounded by it

parts.note: something delightful is lovely

indicators.note: initially signals taking only the opening letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what falls outside anything special and delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: something untidy is precisely what is not special or delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and careless in appearance is the meaning, which is the very opposite of special and delightful.

clue.text: Is work of the writer taken up in whole conference?

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go inside the whole word

parts.note: a sum is a whole or total

indicators.note: in a down answer, taken up means the run of pieces is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
of the writer is the setter's, MY

explanation.surface: A writer asks whether their work is included at a whole conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a formal meeting or conference for discussing a subject is a symposium.

clue.text: Absence from duties, note — it'll make a general change

parts.note: leave is time off work, an absence from duties

explanation.surface: A note about taking time away from work that will change things overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is not a soldier: a raising agent changes the whole mass of dough, and figuratively anything that pervades and transforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A raising agent such as yeast spreads through dough and transforms it throughout, so it effects a general change.

clue.text: Very old partner — one is out to misbehave like a sort of litigant

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: the letters misbehave by running out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very old ex-partner who is out to cause trouble, like someone in court.
explanation.walkthrough: A vexatious litigant, in British law, is someone who repeatedly brings groundless lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone who keeps bringing groundless legal actions to harass others.

clue.text: A range of farm animals revealed in different views of letters

parts.note: a nag is a horse, one farm animal
rams are male sheep, more farm animals

explanation.surface: A variety of livestock shows the farm in different lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range of' signals a mix of animals: a horse plus some sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearrangements of a word's letters offer new readings of the same letters, a different view of them.

clue.text: Endless whisky on the rocks reveals bitterness

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the whisky word is removed

parts.note: a malt is a malt whisky
a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: Drinking whisky over ice without end leads to resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: ill will or spite, a desire to harm, is malice, closely akin to bitterness.

clue.text: College hostility over a University building with grandeur

parts.note: hate is hostility

explanation.surface: A college quarrels with a university over a grand building.
explanation.definitionFit: A French country house or castle, usually large and stately, is a chateau.

clue.text: Old King in agitation, cutting off Prince for not eating properly

indicators.note: the old king pieces cut into the agitation word, sitting inside it
cutting off the prince means removing the letter for prince

parts.note: panic is a state of agitation
REX is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch, flustered after cutting off his son, has stopped eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes the P from the agitation word, leaving ANIC, which the old king then cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering from the eating disorder that makes them refuse food is described with this adjective.

clue.text: I will have way with role, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will get their way with a particular role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the definition: the plural a monarch uses for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch speaking of themselves as 'we' uses a plural in place of the singular first person.

clue.text: American vessel turning up in contest — absorbing stuff

indicators.note: the reversed ship letters go inside the contest word

parts.note: a tie is a match or contest, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the ship prefix is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels

explanation.surface: An American ship turns up during a contest that grips everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' looks like 'gripping'; it describes the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft paper that soaks up liquid, such as a paper handkerchief, is tissue.

clue.text: What activates set progs anytime?

indicators.note: activating sets the letters moving, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what starts a computer's programs running whenever wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progs' is short for programs, which fits the reading: the fodder is the whole of 'set progs anytime'.
explanation.definitionFit: The core software of a computer, such as Windows or Linux, is what launches and manages its programs.

clue.text: Place at the meeting-point of tameness and excitement

indicators.note: only the letters where the two outer words meet survive, the tail of the first and the head of the last; everything else is dropped

explanation.surface: A place where tameness and excitement come together.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London, with a reputation for brash fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Essex is a county in eastern England, a place on the map.

clue.text: Less important Greek character avoiding creature of Greek legend

indicators.note: the monster's name avoids the Greek letter, which is removed from it

parts.note: the Minotaur was the bull-headed monster of the Cretan labyrinth
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A minor Greek figure keeps clear of a monster from myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something of lesser importance or rank is minor.

clue.text: Time to escape from 20 children

indicators.note: the letter for time gets out of the referenced answer, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: the answer to 20 down is the word for absorbing stuff, used here as the starting word

explanation.surface: It is time for the children to get away from something.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal and biblical language, offspring are a person's issue.

clue.text: Unambitious shops a drag in confines of Surbiton

indicators.note: the shopping and pulling pieces sit within the outer letters of the place name
the confines are the edges, so only the first and last letters of Surbiton are used

parts.note: a mall is a set of shops
a tow is a pull or drag

explanation.surface: Shopping is a chore in a dull suburban place like Surbiton.
explanation.walkthrough: Surbiton is a suburb in south-west London, often used as a byword for suburban dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes narrow, provincial outlooks, so it serves as an adjective for lacking ambition.

clue.text: Team, regularly restricting routine starting line-up, backed particular combination

indicators.note: backed means the whole assembled string is read from the end to the start
the second and fourth letters of team hem in the routine and line-up pieces
regularly means every other letter of team is taken

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
a team's starting eleven is written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sports team backs a particular line-up after keeping to its routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes E and M from Team; with the routine and line-up inside, the string ERUTXIM is 'backed' to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of several things combined in a given proportion is a mixture.

clue.text: Poet in series about writers

indicators.note: the series abbreviation goes around the writing implements

parts.note: pens are things that write

explanation.surface: A poet appears in a series about authors.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Edmund Spenser, the sixteenth-century English poet, author of The Faerie Queene.
